argument.text: Fix k,A and a. For a>0 apply M002 with X=Eucl(k), exponent a and set A. At each finite positive scale r every admissible set has finite diameter, so its native extended diameter power is exactly the real diameter power in H; an empty member costs 0 in both conventions, and 0^a=0. Finite families may be padded by empty sets, and any countable family can be enumerated by N (with empty padding when necessary). The additional scale r=infinity in M002 cannot increase the supremum over finite positive scales: its infimum is at most the infimum at any finite scale. Thus M002 gives H^a(A)=muH(a)(A). This argument is for every a>0.

argument.text: Under temporary premise L1: a<dimH(A), M003 gives muH(a)(A)=infinity, and F001 converts this to H^a(A)=infinity. Discharge L1, retaining that implication. Under temporary premise L2: a>dimH(A), M004 gives muH(a)(A)=0, and F001 converts this to H^a(A)=0. Discharge L2, retaining that implication. Eucl(k) has its Borel measurable structure by definition, and the arbitrary a>0 supplies the nonnegative-real source exponent in both applications. Universal introduction of a>0 yields the two clauses in F002.

produces.statement: For every v>0, v<dimH(A) implies H^v(A)=infinity, and dimH(A)<v implies H^v(A)=0.

argument.text: For a>0, if H^a(A)=0, the alternative dimH(A)>a contradicts the infinite-measure clause of F002. Thus dimH(A)≤a. If H^a(A)=infinity, the alternative dimH(A)<a contradicts the zero-measure clause, hence dimH(A)≥a. Nonnegativity follows from the [0,infinity]-valued supremum defining dimH. All these are implications with their displayed antecedents retained, not extra ambient assumptions. Since k,A and a>0 were arbitrary, universally quantify them to record F003, the full normalization and critical-exponent statements for every Euclidean set and positive exponent.

produces.statement: For every nonnegative integer k0, every Z⊆Eucl(k0) and every v>0: H^v(Z)=muH(v)(Z); v<dimH(Z) implies H^v(Z)=infinity; dimH(Z)<v implies H^v(Z)=0; H^v(Z)=0 implies dimH(Z)≤v; H^v(Z)=infinity implies dimH(Z)≥v; and dimH(Z)≥0.

argument.text: Under the temporary premise L3: A⊆B, every delta-cover of B is a delta-cover of A, whence H^v_delta(A)≤H^v_delta(B) and H^v(A)≤H^v(B), for every v>0. If dimH(A)>dimH(B), choose a positive real exponent strictly between them; this is possible also if dimH(A)=infinity, since the smaller dimension must then be finite. The critical statements just established would give infinity=H^v(A)≤H^v(B)=0, a contradiction. This proves dimension monotonicity, discharging L3 with the antecedent A⊆B retained.

Under L4: g:A→Eucl(l) preserves distances, intersect each ambient cover with A, map its members by g, and use these images to cover g(A). Conversely intersect a cover of g(A) with g(A) and take inverse images under g. Distance preservation makes g injective, and both constructions do not increase any member's diameter. Thus the two H^v_delta contents, and then the two H^v measures, are equal for every v>0 and delta>0. The same between-exponents contradiction as in S004 shows dimH(g(A))=dimH(A). This also treats empty A, whose contents vanish and dimension is 0. Discharge L4 and quantify k,A,l,g and retain each stated conditional premise to obtain every clause of the exported claim.

argument.text: H003 says E is compact. Compact subsets of Euclidean space are bounded: the open balls centered at the origin with positive integer radii cover the space, so a finite subcover of E puts it inside one such ball. Hence there exists a real L>0 with E⊆[-L,L]^n. Record this existence before choosing L.

produces.statement: There exists L0>0 such that E⊆[-L0,L0]^n.

argument.text: Choose L as in F001 and set C=(2L+2)^n. By H001, n≥0; first take the branch L1: n≥1. For 0<h≤1, divide each coordinate interval [-L,L] into at most ceil(2L/h) closed intervals of length at most h. The resulting grid contains at most (2L/h+1)^n≤C h^(-n) cubes, each of diameter at most sqrt(n) h, and covers E. For any s>n the total s-cost is at most C n^(s/2) h^(s-n), which tends to zero as h decreases to zero. At each fixed target scale take h≤delta/sqrt(n) and then h arbitrarily small; H^s_delta(E)=0 at every scale, hence H^s(E)=0. N001 yields D≤s for every s>n, so D≤n. N001 also gives 0≤D. This proves the branch L1 implication; discharge L1.

produces.statement: If n≥1, then 0≤D≤n.

argument.text: For the other branch L2: n=0, H002 and the single empty tuple give E=Eucl(0), a singleton. A singleton cover has diameter 0 and zero s-cost for every s>0, so H^s(E)=0 for all s>0. N001 gives D≤s for every s>0, and D≥0, hence D=0. Discharge L2. Since the nonnegative integer n is either zero or at least one, the two branches and F002 give 0≤D≤n, in particular finite D.

produces.statement: 0≤D≤n and D is finite.

argument.text: Finally let s>0 and delta>0. The family of open balls centered at points of E with radius delta/4 covers E. By H003 it has a finite subcover. Each such ball has diameter at most delta/2≤delta, and its s-cost is finite; for n=0 its diameter is 0. Thus this finite admissible cover has finite total cost, so H^s_delta(E)<infinity. Together with F003 this is the exported claim.

For any a>1, divide I into N equal closed intervals, where N ranges through the positive integers. Their corresponding copies in F have diameter 1/N, total a-cost N(1/N)^a=N^(1-a) tending to zero, and mesh tending to zero. Thus H^a(F)=0: at each fixed delta, sufficiently large N are admissible and their costs tend to zero. N001 gives dimH(F)≤a for every a>1, hence dimH(F)≤1=D+1. Discharge L1.

argument.text: For the remaining branch introduce L2: n≥1, and fix q with temporary premise L3: q>D. N002 gives D≥0, so q>0. N001 gives H^q(E)=0 and therefore H^q_r(E)=0 at any r>0. For arbitrary r in (0,1] and epsilon>0, the infimum defining H^q_r supplies a countable r-cover of cost <epsilon/2. Discard empty members. Each nonempty member of diameter zero is a singleton. Replace its i-th occurrence by a Euclidean ball centered at that singleton, of positive diameter ≤r and q-cost <epsilon 2^(-i-2). Such a ball exists since n≥1, and arbitrarily small positive radii have positive diameter and q-cost tending to zero. Keep the other members. Their total cost is <epsilon/2+epsilon sum_{i≥0}2^(-i-2)=epsilon. This proves existence of a countable cover of E by nonempty members with positive diameters ≤r and total q-cost <epsilon.

For any two points in a member of W, the squared Euclidean distance is at most r_i^2+r_i^2. Thus each member has diameter ≤sqrt(2) r_i≤sqrt(2) r.

Each f_i is a nonnegative Borel measurable function: J_i is open and the coefficient rho_i^s is finite. Thus it is almost-everywhere measurable for lambda restricted to I.

argument.text: For the lower estimate fix 0<s<1 and delta>0. Let V be any countable family and introduce L1: it is a delta-cover of I. Enumerate with empty padding and let T⊆N index the nonempty members. Put rho_i=diam(V_i)≤delta. Each V_i is a bounded nonempty subset of R, so sup V_i-inf V_i=rho_i. For any epsilon>0 define J_i=(inf V_i-epsilon 2^(-i-2),sup V_i+epsilon 2^(-i-2)). These open intervals contain V_i and have length rho_i+epsilon 2^(-i-1). Thus they cover I and are Borel measurable.

produces.statement: I⊆union_{i in T}J_i, and each J_i is an open bounded interval of length rho_i+epsilon 2^(-i-1).

argument.text: Apply M005 to Lebesgue measure lambda, the countable index type T, and the intervals J_i. Measure monotonicity and F002 yield 1=lambda(I)≤lambda(union_i J_i)≤sum_i lambda(J_i)=sum_i(rho_i+epsilon 2^(-i-1))≤sum_i rho_i+epsilon. If sum_i rho_i is infinite then sum_i rho_i≥1 already; otherwise let epsilon decrease to zero. The V,rho and T do not depend on epsilon, so sum_i rho_i≥1 in all cases.

produces.statement: sum_{i in T}rho_i≥1.

argument.text: Because 0<s<1 and 0≤rho_i≤delta, rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)rho_i: for rho_i>0 divide by rho_i and use the decreasing power with negative exponent s-1; for rho_i=0 both sides are zero. Hence sum_i rho_i^s≥delta^(s-1)sum_i rho_i≥delta^(s-1) by F003. Discharge L1 and take the infimum over all delta-covers V. This proves H^s_delta(I)≥delta^(s-1) for every delta>0.

produces.statement: For every d0>0, H^s_d0(I)≥d0^(s-1).

argument.text: Since s-1<0, delta^(s-1) tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero, and F004 implies H^s(I)=infinity. By N001, dimH(I)≥s for every s∈(0,1). Letting s increase to 1 gives dimH(I)≥1. Combining with F001 proves dimH(I)=1, with no missing zero-dimensional ambient case.

applications.bindings: Source X=R; G is the type of measures on R, with its usual function-like outer-measure-class structure; nu=lambda; countable source index type=T⊆N; W(i)=J_i.
hypothesis_checks: Lebesgue measure lambda is a measure by D009; measures carry their standard function-like outer-measure-class structure.
T is a subset of N by S002, hence countable.

locals.declaration: Choose x0∈E by the original nonemptiness H002.
Define g(t)=(x0,t) under the Euclidean identification.

argument.text: H002 supplies a point x0∈E. Define g:I→Eucl(n+1) by g(t)=(x0,t). The Euclidean distance between g(t) and g(u) is sqrt(0+|t-u|^2)=|t-u|, so g preserves distances. Its image is contained in F by x0∈E and the definition F=E×I. N001 gives dimH(g(I))=dimH(I) and dimH(F)≥dimH(g(I)). N006 gives dimH(I)=1, hence dimH(F)≥1. Under the temporary premise L1: D=0, this reads dimH(F)≥1=D+1. Discharge L1; x0 is absent from the output. This proves the exported claim for all n, including n=0.

N002 gives the finite real value D≥0, so either D>0 or D=0. N005 gives dimH(F)≥D+1 in the first case, and N007 gives the same bound in the second. Case elimination therefore gives dimH(F)≥D+1 unconditionally. N003 gives the reverse bound, so dimH(F)=D+1. Substituting F=E×I, I=[0,1] and D=dimH(E), with the Euclidean product identification of D001, yields dim_H(E×[0,1])=dim_H E+1. These bounds apply for every original nonempty compact E⊆R^n and every n≥0, as required.
